resolvedFinding: Reused prefixes could expose obsolete or disabled objects. Paginated exact-key admission now rejects unexpected/duplicate keys before HTTP or S3 writes, then requires the complete exact set after staging; no deletion or overwrite.
reasoning: Only trusted accepted enabled latest catalog routes are selected; binding identity, revision, byte bounds and hashes are checked. Literal slash-ending index alias preserves latest page URL.
Every source body is authenticated before writes. Conditional S3 creation and exact body/metadata/header/encryption readback prevent overwriting a conflicting snapshot.
Source download stays attachment; private state, disabled threads and older revisions are not selected. Helper never changes CloudFront.
Quiescent catalog equality before origin switch is an explicit operational gate; source alone does not establish deployment or indefinite hosting.

validation.coverage: Current routes/slash alias; disabled selection; binding/traversal/duplicate rejection; unexpected object on paginator page2 before fetch/write; incomplete final destination.

limits: HTTP/S3 interactions are not live-tested by these focused tests. Actual authenticated staging/readback, quiescent catalog comparison, distribution deployment and public URL/header checks remain required.
Exclusive operator ownership of immutable publication prefix must continue through handover; no concurrent publication writer authorized.
